{{short description|Ancient Greek mathematician}}
'''Nicoteles of Cyrene''' ({{langx|el|Νικοτέλης ὁ Κυρηναῖος}}) ({{circa|250 BC}}) was a [[Greeks|Greek]] [[mathematician]] from [[Cyrene, Libya|Cyrene]].

He is mentioned in the preface to Book 4 of the ''Conics'' of [[Apollonius of Perga|Apollonius]], as criticising [[Conon of Samos|Conon]] concerning the maximum number of points with which a [[conic section]] can meet another conic section. Apollonius states that Nicoteles claimed that the case in which a conic section meets opposite sections could be solved, but had not demonstrated how.<ref>{{cite book |author1=Fabio Acerbi |editor1-last=Keyser |editor1-first=Paul |editor2-last=Scarborough |editor2-first=John |date=2018 |title=The Oxford Handbook of Science and Medicine in the Classical World |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780199734146 |doi=10.1093/oxfordhb/9780199734146.013.69 |pages=269–292 |chapter=Hellenistic Mathematics}}</ref>

It is possible that Nicoteles could be a misspelling of [[Nicomedes (mathematician)|Nicomedes]].{{cn|date=August 2025}}
